newsitem.title: INDONESIA: East Timor guerrillas kill six in ambush - report.
newsitem.headline: East Timor guerrillas kill six in ambush - report.

text.p: East Timorese guerrillas killed a senior local government official, an aide and four security guards in an ambush in the Indonesian-ruled territory, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Thursday.

The daily quoted Indonesian military officials as saying that at least five people were wounded in the attack and in another ambush on Monday at a village near Viqueque town, some 120 km (75 miles) south of Dili, the capital of East Timor.

It identified one of the victims as Eugenio da Costa, the head of the Viqueque regency's administrative affairs department. It said the others killed included another government official and four of da Costa's bodyguards.
Authorities in East Timor were not immediately available for comment.
Military officials were quoted as saying the attackers were part of a small band of guerrillas fighting for the independence of East Timor.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the following year in an act not recognised by the United Nations, which still considers former colonial ruler Portugal as the administering power.

The officials said the attackers fired at a pickup da Costa was driving. The vehicle spun out of control into a ditch and at least one of the victims died of stab wounds, indicating the rebels then attacked the survivors, the officers said.
Later, the guerrillas ambushed another vehicle in the same area, wounding three employees of a company working on a development project in the region, the newspaper said.
Military officials have in the past said the number of armed rebels in the territory is dwindling and that they do not number more than 200 poorly equipped fighters.
Reported attacks by the rebels are rare.
